status: provisional — pending owner/TLF decisions D3 (transport), D4 (receipt), D5 (scopes), D8 (human approval); not an adopted profile

transport.binding: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures, one signature labelled 'aria'
transport.label: aria
transport.nonce: a single-use receiver challenge, fresh for every request, lookups included

headers.aria-credential: sf-string: the exact credential document URL, with parameter digest=:<sha-256 of its canonical JSON>:
headers.aria-audience: sf-string: the receiver DID the request is for
headers.aria-operation: sf-string: the logical operation id (UUID), the same on every retry

retrieval.refusals: problem documents, unsigned: a retrieval produces no receipt

semanticHeaders: every semantic header the descriptor declares and the request carries is covered after the class components, and enters the fingerprint
authenticationOrder: 400 aria.request_invalid: a supported method and exactly one described operation (method and exact path)
400: body rules of the class; for unsafe-body, the descriptor's one media type after normalisation
400: only declared query parameters, each at most once; retrieval names one operation UUID
400: ARIA-Operation exactly once as a UUID sf-string on receiptable classes, absent on retrieval
401 signature: exactly one signature, labelled aria
401 unsigned_operation | digest | signature: covered components are exactly the required ones, without parameters or repeats
401 signature | window: parameters exactly created, expires, nonce, keyid, alg, tag; window at most 60 s and current within the skew
401 digest: Content-Digest sha-256 of the exact content
401 challenge: the nonce is a challenge this receiver issued, unexpired and unconsumed
401 credential: the exact credential named, its digest, keyid equal to its holderKey.id, the key acceptable
401 signature: strict Ed25519 over the base rebuilt from the receiver's configured origin
the challenge is consumed atomically; the request is authenticated
403 aria.audience_mismatch: the first admission check (signed rejected/attempt, or a problem document for retrieval)
ed25519: holder key canonical, not small order, torsion free; R canonical, not small order, torsion free; S < L; then RFC 8032 verification (both equations then agree)

fingerprint.algorithm: sha-256 over the ARIA canonical JSON of the object below, written sha-256=:<base64>:

object.path: the exact path, without the query
object.query: object of the descriptor's query parameters present, name to value
object.mediaType: the descriptor's one media type, lowercase, parameters sorted (unsafe-body only)
object.semanticHeaders: object of the descriptor's semantic headers present, lowercase name to value
object.contentDigest: RFC 9530 sha-256 of the body; of empty content for unsafe-empty; absent for safe classes

receipt.signed: the ARIA canonical JSON of the receipt with proof.value removed (proof.alg and proof.keyid are signed)
receipt.dataModel: objects, strings and integers only; no duplicate keys; no unknown members

aria.authentication_failed.note: challenge covers replay: a consumed challenge is refused

aria.operation_unknown.note: retrieval of an operation with no record; the client keeps it unknown

receiverReasons: namespaced <ns>.<name>: resource authorization in admission (403, attempt), business rules after the claim (422, operation)

atpMapping.ATP-200: admission allow (flagged in monitor/warn); never a receipt state

scopes: D5 provisional: new grants are namespace:resource:action, three lowercase segments, no @version; 1.0 documents are read under their own pattern (two or more segments); credential scopes compare exactly, never as patterns; receiver policy patterns may end in :* and a matching deny wins
approval: D8 provisional: refuse — a missing approval rejects the attempt and claims nothing; holding for approval is deferred
reconciliation: an uncertain failure marks the claim, by compare-and-set, and keeps it locked; a release names the exact claim observed and an assurance that the old work cannot apply its effect later (transactional: the effect commits only with its recorded outcome; fenced: an external adapter guarantees final absence and that the old work cannot commit); an unmarked claim, a missing assurance or an observation of an earlier claim releases nothing; effects are counted when they land, apart from the record
admissionLifetime: an admission is judged when made and again when used: after the resource authorizer, before a claim is granted and after the storage write; it keeps its status evidence and approval and expires with its request (signature expires plus skew); a lookup is judged again before its receipts are released
revocationLookup: D4 provisional: a revoked credential authorizes no lookup; a currently valid credential of the same DID may retrieve the original receipt; revocation never deletes or reclassifies the operation
